Nail thickening over the pigmented band
Pigment extending to the proximal nail fold
key_facts: New pigmented lesion on the left second toenail
Lesion first appeared 12 months before presentation
Lesion was progressively growing
Asymptomatic
No prior treatments attempted
Otherwise well
Denied fevers or weight loss
Nail thickening over the pigmented band
Pigment was the same width throughout the band
No other nail or skin lesions found

shortlist.label: Melanonychia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive pigmented nail lesion with nail thickening

shortlist.label: Onychomatricoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix

shortlist.label: Nail matrix nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented lesion with corresponding nail thickening

shortlist.label: Subungual hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis present

shortlist.label: Onychocytic matricoma
shortlist.why_kept: Villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate

raw.rationale: The presence of a bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix, villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate, and the absence of melanocytic lesions or atypia support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Melanonychia
rejected.why: No melanocytic lesions were observed, and immunostaining was negative for S100, which is typically positive in melanocytic lesions.

rejected.label: Nail matrix nevus
rejected.why: Histopathologic examination did not show melanocytic proliferation, which is characteristic of nail matrix nevi.

rejected.label: Subungual hematoma
rejected.why: The presence of a progressive, asymptomatic lesion with nail thickening and the specific histopathologic findings do not support a diagnosis of subungual hematoma, which is typically associated with trauma and hemorrhage.

rejected.label: Onychocytic matricoma
rejected.why: While onychocytic matricoma could be considered due to the location and some histological features, the specific combination of findings, especially the villous fibroepithelial projections and the absence of significant keratinocyte atypia, points more towards onychomatricoma.
